title: Checks for usage of Debug formatting.
summary: The purpose of this lint is to catch debugging remnants. The purpose of the Debug trait is to facilitate debugging Rust code, and no guarantees are made about its output. It should not be used in user-facing output. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for unnecessary repetition of structure name when a replacement with Self is applicable.
summary: Unnecessary repetition. Mixed use of Self and struct name feels inconsistent. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the use of bindings with a single leading underscore.
summary: A single leading underscore is usually used to indicate that a binding will not be used. Using such a binding breaks this expectation. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the use of item with a single leading underscore.
summary: A single leading underscore is usually used to indicate that a item will not be used. Using such a item breaks this expectation. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of .as_ref() or .as_mut() where the types before and after the call are the same.
summary: The call is unnecessary. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for extern crate and use items annotated with lint attributes.
summary: Lint attributes have no effect on crate imports. Most likely a ! was forgotten. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Detects format!-style macros (e.g. format!, println!, write!) where an argument is passed with an explicit & but the value is already a reference, resulting in a double reference (e.g. &&T).
summary: The extra & is redundant and can make the code less clear. Format macros take references to the arguments internally, so passing &x when x is already a reference produces a double reference. The compiler is currently unable to optimize double references, which results in about 6% degradation per call. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks that the concat! macro has at least two arguments.
summary: If there are less than 2 arguments, then calling the macro is doing nothing. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for Into, TryInto, From, TryFrom, or IntoIterator calls which uselessly convert to the same type.
summary: Redundant code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for the use of format!("string literal with no argument") and format!("{}", foo) where foo is a string.
summary: There is no point of doing that. format!("foo") can be replaced by "foo".to_owned() if you really need a String. The even worse &format!("foo") is often encountered in the wild. format!("{}", foo) can be replaced by foo.clone() if foo: String or foo.to_owned() if foo: &str. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for variable declarations immediately followed by a conditional affectation.
summary: This is not idiomatic Rust. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for NonZero*::new_unchecked() being used in a const context.
summary: Using NonZero*::new_unchecked() is an unsafe function and requires an unsafe context. When used in a context evaluated at compilation time, NonZero*::new().unwrap() will provide the same result with identical runtime performances while not requiring unsafe. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for transmutes to the original type of the object and transmutes that could be a cast.
summary: Readability. The code tricks people into thinking that something complex is going on. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of vec![..] when using [..] would be possible.
summary: This is less efficient. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.
